alternatives.option: Host-attested prompt alone counts as a ruling
alternatives.reason_rejected: a prompt proves a human typed something, not that they hold authority over the scope; kept as human_statement only

context: Dave ruled on the foundation programme plan (2026-09-15): RB1 parallel CLI lane, RB2 absorb W2/2.17.x, RB3 his other computer for C28, RB4 Codex installed locally (0.154.0), RB6 signed ceremony + host-attested statements, RB7 long-lived foundation/v3 branch. Execution starts.
rationale: Dave accepted the recommendation 2026-09-15. R03 forbids model-written text or caller-controlled fields from establishing human authority; the ceremony gives authenticated rulings a boundary enforced outside generated prose, and human_statement preserves the human's literal words with honest uncertainty. Known ergonomic cost: a coordinator cannot mint rulings from chat.
summary: RB6 ruled: human rulings are produced only by an interactive signed CLI ceremony the model cannot invoke (TTY required, human key outside any repo), and host-attested literal human prompts are captured as human_statement evidence (unverified authority) that only the ceremony can upgrade; a caller-supplied actor field never confers authority
